gdacs-cyclone-tc-1001347.summary: Typhoon Cempaka (JMA No. 32) began on 6 November 2026 near the Mariana Islands. It passed over waters south of Japan's Ogasawara Islands, where Ogasawara Village issued storm and high wave warnings. Sources report it dissipated or became an extratropical cyclone around 11–12 November. No damage, casualties or evacuations are reported in the sources reviewed.

gdacs-cyclone-tc-1001351.summary: Tropical Cyclone Akvan was listed by an automated alert feed as starting on 16 November 2026 over the Bay of Bengal, near India, with a centre at 13.1 N, 87.3 E and peak winds of 93 km/h. A headline, unverified, says it may become a severe cyclonic storm by 19 November. No news, government or relief reports could be checked, so no impacts are confirmed.

gdacs-drought-dr-1018332.summary: Drought affecting much of Europe, recorded from 21 December 2025. Sources describe severe conditions through late summer and September 2026. Switzerland recorded its driest August since measurements began in 1864. England was declared in drought on 29 July 2026. Wildfires had burned more than 500,000 hectares across the EU by 31 August 2026. Conditions in November 2026 are not confirmed.

gdacs-drought-dr-1023877.summary: Drought affecting Northern South America and the Panama Isthmus. The feed gives a start of 21 September 2022, but another source lists 21 February 2026 to 20 October 2026, and this could not be reconciled. Colombia's weather agency said October's wet season was not normal. The Panama Canal cut daily transits from 38 to 32 because of falling water levels. Panama declared a nationwide emergency on 25 August 2026. Latest update 20 November 2026; ongoing.

Ethiopia's IFRC GO operation reports onset delays of up to 4 weeks in parts of the country. No end date has been reported.

gdacs-earthquake-eq-1578540.summary: A M5.9 earthquake struck northwestern China at 10:45 UTC on 21 November 2026, at a depth of 10 km according to USGS. USGS places the epicentre at 37.196°N, 96.640°E, though other sources give different locations. No affected places, casualties or damage have been reported in the sources checked, and official Chinese sources were not retrieved. The latest feed update was at 12:51 UTC that day.

gdacs-flood-fl-1104239.summary: Flooding has affected Selangor, Perak and Pahang, according to reports dated 5 to 10 November 2026. Eight people were swept away at Sungai Pertak in Kuala Kubu Bharu on 9 November; five bodies have been found and three remain missing. Evacuee numbers fell in Selangor but rose in Perak. A flood warning covers Jerantut and Rompin from 11 to 14 November. Cash aid payments for affected Selangor households were due to begin on 10 November.

Latest status could not be confirmed.

ifrc-earthquake-8060.summary: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck offshore off Nagekeo Regency, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, on 15 August 2026, according to an automated alert feed. The reports could not be verified against news, government or humanitarian sources, and the current status is not confirmed.

The latest dated report found is from late July 2026, and the current status is not reported.

ifrc-flood-8050.summary: Monsoon flooding in Myanmar began in August 2026, affecting parts of Sagaing, Ayeyarwady, Rakhine, Kachin and northwest Myanmar. UNICEF estimated about 600,000 people affected as of end of August. Mapping showed inundation in Ayeyarwady in mid-September 2026. Status as of 21 November 2026 is not reported.

ifrc-flood-8073.summary: On 26 August 2026, a flash flood struck Rasuwa district in Nepal's Bagmati Province, damaging settlements, markets, roads, bridges and hydropower facilities. Government estimates put 84,270 people in 17 municipalities across six districts as affected. Recovery and response are ongoing; the latest dated item found is from 19 November 2026. Death toll figures conflict across sources.

news-flood-flood-ps-3d066bfa68.summary: Heavy rain and flooding hit Gaza from 7 November 2026, flooding shelters and tents across the Strip. A sand embankment collapsed onto tents in Deir al-Balah on 8 November, killing five people. Health Ministry figures say 350,000 displaced people were sleeping in the open as of 9 November. Rescue searches for missing people were continuing on 9 November.
